description.en: Azerbaijan observes public holidays reflecting its national independence, Islamic traditions, and Azerbaijani cultural heritage.

sections.title: About Azerbaijan
sections.content: Azerbaijan, officially the Republic of Azerbaijan, is a transcontinental landlocked country at the boundary of Western Asia and Eastern Europe. It is a part of the South Caucasus region and is bounded by the Caspian Sea to the east, Russia's republic of Dagestan to the north, Georgia to the northwest, Turkey, via the exclave of Nakhchivan, and Armenia to the west, and Iran to the south. Baku is the capital and largest city.

sections.title: Important Notice
sections.content: Public holiday dates and observance rules can change, especially when holidays fall on weekends. Always confirm critical dates with official Azerbaijan government sources when planning travel, payroll, or business operations.

sections.title: How Azerbaijan's Public Holidays Are Observed
sections.content:
On most public and bank holidays:

Banks and government offices are closed.
Schools are closed.
Some businesses operate reduced hours.
Public transport and retail services may run modified schedules.
Private businesses are not legally required to close but often adjust operating hours.

sections.title: Why Azerbaijan's Public Holidays Matter
sections.content:
Understanding Azerbaijan public holidays helps with:

Business and payroll planning.
School and academic scheduling.
Travel and accommodation planning.
Avoiding service disruptions.
Both residents and visitors benefit from knowing when closures and peak travel periods are likely.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in Azerbaijan?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in Azerbaijan?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in Azerbaijan?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in Azerbaijan?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in Azerbaijan?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
